rationale: The original oral cold-pressed flaxseed oil comparison shows less anxiety-like avoidance in a healthy mouse light–dark test. The exact preparation and behavioral endpoint allow a minimal easing signal. Small animal groups, possible locomotor effects, unmatched saline and unclear elevated-plus-maze reporting limit transfer. An oil-only human trial is imprecise, and milk-vehicle and other model findings are mixed. No separate Parkinson anxiety effect is established.

An authenticated investigator thesis summary and indexed article clarify acute ON medians of 150 and 270 minutes with the ground-soy comparison. Post-180-minute data were self-recorded. The tested preparation and outcome do not isolate refined soybean oil or daily OFF time. The frozen clinical direction stays open.

The officially registered grape-seed proanthocyanidin trial reports within-arm sleep change at abstract depth. The primary placebo-relative insomnia table is unavailable. The separate SNACk registration does not identify the oil or provide results. Neither supplies a refined grapeseed oil Parkinson insomnia estimate.

A small randomized trial found a favorable immediate postexercise fatigue contrast for purified red paprika xanthophyll in athletes. The later daily-fatigue registration has no posted outcome values. The measured comparisons do not isolate raw bell pepper or Parkinson fatigue.
